structure.summary: On Christmas Eve in a shabby $8-per-week flat, Della Young weeps over having only $1.87 to buy a gift for her husband, Jim, until she decides to sell her long, beautiful hair to Madame Sofronie for twenty dollars. After running on foot to various stores, she purchases a platinum fob chain for Jim's heirloom gold watch, then returns home to style her remaining hair into short curls while praying he will still find her pretty. When Jim arrives home looking thin and serious, he stares at Della with a peculiar, unreadable expression that terrifies her before she explains she cut her hair to afford his present. The tension breaks when Jim reveals he sold his own gold watch to buy Della a set of expensive tortoise-shell combs, rendering both gifts useless but demonstrating their mutual sacrifice.

characters.physical_description: Della has long, brown hair described as a 'brown cascade' and 'shining brilliantly' before she cuts it. After the sale, her head is covered with 'tiny close-lying curls' making her look like a 'truant schoolboy.' She wears an 'old brown jacket' and 'old brown hat.' She is described as having 'dim eyes' when emotional and her face loses color in moments of fear.

descriptions.text: Della Young is a devoted and sacrificial wife who, despite living in poverty with only $1.87 for Christmas, sells her most prized possession—her long, beautiful hair—to buy a gift for her husband. Her actions are driven by deep love and a desire to bring joy to Jim, even at the cost of her own appearance, culminating in a moment of shared irony and mutual sacrifice.

descriptions.text: Jim is a twenty-two-year-old husband who lives in a shabby flat with his wife, Della, on a reduced income of $20 per week. He possesses a deep, quiet devotion to his wife, demonstrated by his willingness to sell his heirloom gold watch to buy her a gift, even though it renders her gift to him useless. His initial reaction to Della's changed appearance is one of stunned silence and confusion rather than anger or disappointment.

plot_summary.plot_summary:
On Christmas Eve, Della Young weeps in her shabby $8-per-week flat because she has only $1.87 to buy a gift for her husband, Jim. Desperate to find a meaningful present, she decides to sell her long, beautiful hair to Madame Sofronie for twenty dollars. This decision marks the beginning of her journey to secure funds for a gift she believes Jim deserves.

After running on foot to various stores, Della purchases a platinum fob chain specifically for Jim's heirloom gold watch. Upon returning home, she styles her remaining hair into short curls, praying that Jim will still find her pretty despite the drastic change. When Jim arrives home looking thin and serious, he stares at Della with a peculiar, unreadable expression that terrifies her before she explains she cut her hair to afford his present.

The tension breaks when Jim reveals he sold his own gold watch to buy Della a set of expensive tortoise-shell combs, rendering both gifts useless but demonstrating their mutual sacrifice. The story concludes with the couple realizing that their willingness to give up their most prized possessions for one another proves the depth of their love, even though the physical gifts can no longer be used.
